It consumes the metering data as delivered — it must not re-implement any part of the collection pipeline, which is owned by RHAISTRAT-9990 and out of scope here. ## Scope - Compute per-project GPU-hour consumption reports aggregated over administrator-selectable time ranges from the metering data delivered by RHAISTRAT-9990. - Expose the report data through a stable API suitable for retrieval by finance tooling. - Provide CSV export of the reports. - Consume the metering data schema exactly as delivered by RHAISTRAT-9990 (no collection, transformation pipeline, or schema ownership). - Reports are denominated in GPU-hours; currency/cost-rate modelling is out of scope. ## Acceptance Criteria - Given metering data delivered by RHAISTRAT-9990, when an administrator requests a per-project GPU-hour consumption report for a selected time range, then the report is returned with per-project GPU-hour totals for that range. - Reports are retrievable as CSV. - Reports are retrievable via a stable API usable by finance tooling, such that integrations built against it do not break from ordinary report content changes. - The metering data schema from RHAISTRAT-9990 is final and available before report computation is implemented against it (precondition gate; the schema is owned by that strategy and not final until it lands). - No metering collection logic is implemented here; the metering pipeline remains wholly owned by RHAISTRAT-9990. - Report values are in GPU-hours; no dollar/cost-rate conversion is introduced. ## HLR Traceability - HLR-1 (P0): per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges — computation side, computed from RHAISTRAT-9990 metering data. - HLR-2 (P1): reports exportable as CSV and retrievable via a stable API for finance tooling.
